input: The pressure drop values that have been reported for the benchmark material differ by enough to matter for blower sizing, and the difference appears to track the test conditions more closely than it tracks the material itself. One group measured loose powder in a shallow bed and reported the drop across the bed alone, with the entry and exit losses taken out. The other group measured formed bodies in a deeper bed and reported the drop across the whole test section, fittings included. The two figures are therefore not really two measurements of one quantity. A shallow bed of powder and a deep bed of formed bodies differ in voidage and in the flow passages that they present, and the whole-section figure carries end losses that the bed-only figure excludes by construction. Read on those terms, the higher values are the expected outcome of the second arrangement rather than evidence that the material resists flow more strongly in one laboratory than in another. The preference here is for the whole-section values as the design basis, and it rests on one condition: that the duty in service presents the benchmark material as formed bodies in a bed of comparable depth, so that the end losses the figure includes are losses that the plant will also incur. Where the duty is a thin layer or a coated form, the bed-only values are the closer match and the preference reverses.
